title: Normality and divisorial description of a log regular structure
statement: Let $(Y,N,\alpha)$ be a locally Noetherian log regular fs log scheme [def-trf-fs-log-blowup, pqf-def-locnoeth]. Let $V$ be the locus where the characteristic monoid $N/\mathcal O_Y^\times$ is zero, and write $j:V\hookrightarrow Y$. Then $V$ is open dense, every local ring of $Y$ is a normal domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], and the structural map identifies $N$ with the subsheaf $\mathcal O_Y\cap j_*\mathcal O_V^\times$ of the multiplicative sheaf $\mathcal O_Y$. In particular every section of $N$ restricts to a unit on $V$. On an integral affine open $\operatorname{Spec}C\subset Y$, $C$ is integrally closed in its fraction field.

source.place: Expose VI, 1.4, printed p. 69 (dense triviality locus and divisorial equality); Expose VIII, 3.4.1, printed p. 110, and 3.5, printed pp. 114--115 (fs log regular schemes are normal).

proof.text: Fix a geometric point $\bar y$ over $y$, set $A_0=\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ and $A=\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{Y,\bar y}$, and choose a sharp chart $P=\overline N_{\bar y}\to N$ on an affine pointed etale neighbourhood $W$ by the sharp-chart lemma. In particular $P$ is finitely generated, integral, saturated and sharp. The chart definition gives $N_{\bar y}=P\oplus A^\times$. Replacing that sharp chart and its affine neighbourhood $W$ if necessary, as permitted by the completed-chart lemma (from now on $W$ and $a:P\to A$ denote the replacement), it identifies $\widehat A$, respecting these monomials, with the complete monoid model $B_k(P,n)$ if $A$ contains a field, and with $B_C(P,n)/(\theta)$ otherwise. By normality of these saturated models, $\widehat A$ is a normal domain. This is only the fs case: no saturation of a non-saturated log scheme is introduced.

source.place: VI 1.6, printed p. 70; saturated complete-model normality input from Kato (1994), 4.1, WANTED.

proof.text: By the affine strict-local comparison lemma, applied to an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}D\ni y$ (so $D_{\mathfrak p}=A_0$) and the separable closure $K$ of $\kappa(y)$ in $\Omega$, $A$ is isomorphic as an $A_0$-algebra to an algebraic strict henselization $A_0^{\mathrm{sh}}$ relative to $K$, by a local isomorphism. Its index pairs $(S,\chi:S\to K)$ are the pointed etale triples $(S,\ker\chi,\text{induced }\kappa(\ker\chi)\to K)$ over the closed point, with the same morphisms, so $A_0^{\mathrm{sh}}$ is the triples colimit of the two lemmas below. Hence $A_0\to A$ and $A\to\widehat A$ ($\widehat A$ the completion at the maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_{A_0}A$) are faithfully flat, by the strict-henselization and completed-strict-henselization lemmas (their Noetherian hypothesis holds because $Y$ is locally Noetherian). Descend normal-domainness along each map, as follows. For a faithfully flat $E\to F$ with $F$ a normal domain, ideal contraction for the zero ideal makes $E\to F$ injective, so $E$ is a domain. If $a/b\in\operatorname{Frac}E$ is integral over $E$, its image is integral over $F$ by the same monic equation, hence lies in $F$. Thus $a\in bF\cap E=bE$ by ideal contraction, so $a/b\in E$. Apply this argument first to $A\to\widehat A$ and then to $A_0\to A$. All local rings of $Y$ are therefore normal domains.

source.place: VI 1.6, followed by explicit faithfully flat descent; ideal contraction is Stacks Tag 00HE.

proof.text: On the chart $W$, choose generators $p_1,\ldots,p_r$ of $P$ and put $s=\prod_i a(p_i)$, with empty product $1$. The associated-log chart formula says that the characteristic is zero exactly where all these generators are units. Hence $V\times_Y W=D(s)$, an open subset of $W$. Etale maps are open, so their images show that $V$ is open in $Y$. Apply monoidal-ideal contraction at $\bar y$ to the empty monoid ideal: no $a(p)$ is zero in $A$, and therefore $s\neq0$ in the domain $A$ of step 2. Thus $D(s)\subset\operatorname{Spec}A$ is nonempty. Every open neighbourhood of the closed point of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ is the whole spectrum; the preimage of every neighbourhood of $y$ contains that closed point, and hence meets $D(s)$. Its image lies in $V$. Since $y$ was arbitrary, $V$ is dense. Every section of $N$ restricts to a unit on $V$, by the chart formula or the definition of the triviality locus.

source.place: Direct argument for VI 1.4, printed p. 69: finite generators, principal open, and nonvanishing monomials.

proof.text: The structural map is injective on the geometric stalk at $\bar y$. Indeed, if $u a(p)=v a(q)$ with $u,v\in A^\times$, then $(a(p))=(a(q))$. Contraction of the monoid ideals $p+P$ and $q+P$ gives $p+P=q+P$. Thus $p=q+r$ and $q=p+t$ for $r,t\in P$; integrality gives $r+t=0$, and sharpness gives $r=t=0$, so $p=q$. Since $a(p)\neq0$ in the domain $A$, cancellation gives $u=v$. Together with $N_{\bar y}=P\oplus A^\times$, this proves injectivity.

source.place: Direct stalk calculation for VI 1.4; monoidal-ideal contraction is VIII 3.4.3, used only through its separate cited statement.

proof.text: Let a germ of $\mathcal O_Y\cap j_*\mathcal O_V^\times$ at $\bar y$ be represented by a regular function $f$ on a pointed etale neighbourhood, invertible on its intersection with $V$. Refine with the chart neighbourhood of step 1. Pullback of the inverse to $\operatorname{Spec}A[1/s]$ shows that $f$ is a unit in $A[1/s]$. Write an inverse as $g/s^m$. The localization equality gives $s^l(fg-s^m)=0$ for some $l\geq0$; since $A$ is a domain and $s\neq0$, $fg=s^m=a(m\sum_i p_i)$. Pass to the completed monoid model of step 1. The complete-toric monomial-factor lemma, applied to this equation, gives $f=\widehat u\,a(p)$ in $\widehat A$ for some $p\in P$ and $\widehat u\in\widehat A^\times$. The same argument covers $s=1$.

source.place: Direct divisorial recognition for VI 1.4 via VI 1.6: invertibility on the principal open becomes a factorization of a monomial in the complete local model.

proof.text: We have $(f)\widehat A=(a(p))\widehat A$. By faithfully flat ideal contraction along $A\to\widehat A$, both inclusions descend: $f=a(p)u$ and $a(p)=fv$ for some $u,v\in A$. Substitution gives $a(p)=a(p)uv$. Since $a(p)\neq0$ and $A$ is a domain, $uv=1$; hence $u\in A^\times$. Consequently the germ $f$ is the image of $(p,u)\in P\oplus A^\times=N_{\bar y}$. This proves surjectivity onto the intersection at each geometric point; step 4 gives injectivity. The structural map factors through the intersection by step 3. Geometric-stalk detection of isomorphisms of etale sheaves of sets now identifies $N$ with $\mathcal O_Y\cap j_*\mathcal O_V^\times$, compatibly with multiplication and the structural maps.

source.place: Direct descent and sheaf argument for VI 1.4, printed p. 69; not an application of the log-smooth preservation lemma.

proof.text: Let $\operatorname{Spec}C\subseteq Y$ be an integral affine open. For each maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of $C$, the local ring $C_{\mathfrak m}=\mathcal O_{Y,y_{\mathfrak m}}$ is a normal domain by step 2. The local-normality criterion therefore makes $C$ a normal domain, equivalently integrally closed in its fraction field.

source.place: Affine-local consequence of step 2; Stacks Tag 030B, using its existing Mathlib leaf.

lean.statement: theorem logRegular_divisorialStructure (X : FineSaturatedLogScheme.{u}) (hX : X.IsLogRegular) : (∃ U : X.scheme.Opens, Dense (U : Set X.scheme) ∧ X.logStructure.trivialityLocus = (U : Set X.scheme) ∧ Presheaf.IsSheaf X.scheme.smallEtaleTopology (divisorialLogPresheaf U.ι) ∧ ∃ (e : X.logStructure.monoidSheaf.obj ≅ divisorialLogPresheaf U.ι), e.hom ≫ divisorialStructuralMap U.ι = X.logStructure.alpha ∧ ∀ (W : X.scheme.Etale) (s : X.logStructure.monoidSheaf.obj.obj (op W)), IsUnit ((pullback.fst W.hom U.ι).appTop (X.logStructure.alpha.app (op W) s))) ∧ (∀ y : X.scheme, IsDomain (X.scheme.presheaf.stalk y) ∧ IsIntegrallyClosed (X.scheme.presheaf.stalk y)) ∧ (∀ (U : X.scheme.Opens), IsAffineOpen U → IsIntegral U.toScheme → IsIntegrallyClosed (Γ(X.scheme, U)))
